name: hologram
//peer: Whichever app is Jarvis brings its own copy of these; both of them depend on all nine directly. The react entry calls into expo-gl, to draw him, only once it has found expo-gl's native module in the build; and the conversation entry calls into the ElevenLabs SDK (its client's `Conversation.startSession`, which must be the very copy `@elevenlabs/react-native` registers its session strategy on — `mobile/src/agent-audio-track.contract.spec.ts` checks it is) and, for the recorded greeting, LiveKit's audio session and hologram's own native player (expo) on a device, expo-audio in a browser. The native player is why this package has an expo-module.config.json: both apps autolink it.
//exports: Four entries, and the split matters: '.' is the design, the voice tracking, the ElevenLabs credentials and the conversation's framework-free parts, importing nothing from outside the package but types, so it runs headless in the tests, in a browser, and in a client with no React at all. './gpu' is all of him on the GPU — his body's passes and the picture of the rest of him as shader sources, the CPU reference they are held to, the view-basis maths, and a renderer over a bare WebGL 2 context — under the main entry's rule (the context is handed in), so the headset draws it through three.js and a phone or a watch through expo-gl while neither is ever imported here. './react' is the view, which needs React and Reanimated for real, and expo-gl, which it loads on a device only once expo-gl's native module is found. './conversation' needs React and the ElevenLabs SDK but deliberately not expo-gl, so a screen can hold a conversation whether or not the view can draw. './react/sample' is sample mode's clock-made voice, mood toast and frame-rate readout, and './react/lifecycle' the screen-level pieces, both clear of expo-gl for the same reason. './assets/*' is the files themselves, for a bundler that takes a file as a URL rather than as Metro's asset id: the headset imports the greeting as `hologram/assets/greeting.mp3?url` and never reaches './conversation', whose greeting player is Metro's.
